# Aruna

> Aruna is a type-safe networking framework for roblox-ts. You define server actions
> (client → server RPC) and signals (server → client push) once, in TypeScript, with
> schemas; the `aruna build` compiler generates typed client/server stubs, a runtime,
> and a Rojo-buildable project layout. This file is written for coding agents: it
> describes the public API and the things that are easy to get wrong.

## What you are looking at

You are reading this from inside `node_modules/@arunajs/aruna`. This is a published
library. Consumer code imports from four runtime entry points and three generated
virtual modules:

- `aruna/server`  — `defineAction`, `defineSignal`, `createServerApp`, dispatch/validation
- `aruna/client`  — `createClientApp` (argless default transport; can own the signal subscriber via `{ signals, createSubscriber }`), `invokeAction`, `invokeOptimistic` (updates shown until the server's snapshot contains the call)
- `aruna/roblox`  — the RemoteEvent server transport (`robloxRemoteEvent` for `createServerApp({ transport })`), `createActionInvoker`, low-level `bindActions`, signal pub/sub
- `aruna/schema`  — `schema.*` builders + `Infer` (the single schema-inference type)
- `aruna/testing` — the spec surface: `createTestServerApp`, `createTestPlayer`, `describe`/`it`/`expect` (compiled and run by `aruna test`, never part of a game build)
- `aruna/ui` — UI bindings: `createReactBindings(React)` (`useResource`, `useAction`), `createVideBindings({ source, cleanup, batch })` (`resourceState`, `actionState`), and the renderer-agnostic `observeResource`/`peekResource`/`observeAction`. The renderer is passed in; Aruna never imports one
- `$aruna/actions/server` — generated server action registry (`actions`, `defaultRateLimit`)
- `$aruna/actions/client` — generated per-action client call functions
- `$aruna/signals` — generated signal registry (`signals`, `Signals`)
- `$aruna/resources/server` — generated resource registry (`resources`) for `createServerApp({ resources })`
- `$aruna/resources/client` — typed resource bindings (`questProgress.subscribe(...)`), `Resources`

The `aruna/*` and `$aruna/*` specifiers are tsconfig path aliases that `aruna build`
(and `init`, `dev`, `test`, `doctor --fix`) write into the project's `tsconfig.json`,
relative to the file, with no `baseUrl`. They are NOT the npm subpath exports
(`@arunajs/aruna/server`); in a real project you import the short `aruna/*` form.

## Docs

- [Getting started](./docs/getting-started.md): install, project shape, the build loop, a full minimal action round-trip.
- [Actions](./docs/actions.md): `defineAction`, server registration, client calls, rate limits (fixed window or token bucket), the request budget and `onAbuse`, declared `errors` and `ctx.fail`, fire-and-forget, `ctx.player`, `ctx.publisher`, contract change rules.
- [Signals](./docs/signals.md): `defineSignal`, server publisher (`to`/`toMany`/`toAll`), client subscriber, publishing from inside an action (`ctx.publisher` / `createActionDefiner`).
- [Resources](./docs/resources.md): `defineResource`, server-loaded state a client subscribes to, invalidation, load timeouts, what is and is not guaranteed.
- [Stores](./docs/stores.md): `defineStore` / `definePlayerStore`, `StoreResult` error taxonomy, session locking, migrations, `createServerApp({ playerStore })` and `ctx.store`.
- [Schema](./docs/schema.md): every `schema.*` builder, numeric width hints, Roblox userdata (vector3/color3/cframe), inference.
- [UI bindings](./docs/ui.md): `aruna/ui` for React and Vide — reading a resource, a call's pending/error state, `exclusive`, Vide's scope rules, per-call stub options.
- [Observability](./docs/observability.md): `aruna inspect network`, `createNetworkMetrics()`, `onReject`.
- [Shared safety](./docs/shared-safety.md): what code in shared modules may reach, and what the static check cannot see.
- [Testing](./docs/testing.md): `aruna test`, `aruna/testing` (`createTestServerApp`, `createTestPlayer`, `describe`/`it`/`expect`), what the game build does with specs.
- [CLI](./docs/cli.md): `aruna build`/`check`/`init`/`doctor`/`inspect`/`contract`, flags, what each generates.
- [Diagnostics](./docs/diagnostics.md): every `aruna::NNN` code with its name, default severity and meaning, and the `strict` option that changes it.
- [Troubleshooting](./docs/troubleshooting.md): what each common setup error means and how to fix it — native compiler not available or not loaded, TypeScript pin skew, missing rbxtsc, Rojo project not mounting out/, unresolved `$aruna/...` imports and `aruna::111`, Lune missing, Studio sync — and runtime failures: the client waiting on `ArunaRemoteEvent`, `ActionTimeoutError`, masked `ActionInternalError`, rate limits, contract mismatch, the in-memory Studio store, `StoreLockedError`.
- [Before you ship](./docs/production.md): a production checklist — authorization, rate limits, error logging, store readiness and budget, the contract snapshot in CI, deploy skew, and what is not implemented yet.
- [Architecture](./docs/architecture.md): module boundaries, the client/server/shared partition, generated modules, the runtime, binary codec.

## Rules of thumb (read before writing Aruna code)

- Stores are server-only persistence. A failed load NEVER falls back to the default —
  that is how a save file gets overwritten. Handle `{ ok: false }` explicitly, and treat an
  absent `ctx.store` as "not loaded", not "new player". See stores.md.
- Action and signal definitions are discovered by file classification (client/server/shared
  by path convention). Server-only logic must live in server-classified files or the
  compiler reports a boundary violation. See architecture.md.
- Concerns have a file form and a folder form: `actions.ts` or `actions/`, `ui.tsx` or
  `ui/`, and so on. Definitions are found by their `define*` call, so split a concern
  across as many files as you want — no config change, no naming ceremony.
- A domain (`src/domains/<name>/`) keeps its `client/` and `server/` subtrees private.
  Other domains may import its root modules — or only its `index.ts` once it has one —
  and reaching past that reports `aruna::304`. Same-domain and app-shell imports are
  unrestricted. See architecture.md.
- After adding or changing any `defineAction`/`defineSignal`, run `aruna build` — `aruna check`
  does NOT regenerate stubs or the manifest, so client stubs go stale.
- `ctx.player` is always present (wire dispatches carry the caller; in-process
  `app.dispatch` requires a ctx with a player). Import `defineAction` from
  `aruna/roblox` to get `ctx.player: Player` typing. Test actions through
  `createServerApp(...).dispatch(actionId, { player }, input)`.
- To publish a signal from inside an action, use `ctx.publisher` (injected when
  `createServerApp` owns a publisher). Bind `createActionDefiner<Signals, Player>()`
  in a shared module for a non-optional, registry-checked `ctx.publisher`.
- Do not hand-wire `tsconfig.json` for Aruna: like Next.js, the build keeps it correct
  (it forces the roblox-ts compile contract and the aliases, adds defaults only where a
  key is unset, and edits in place). Do not add a `baseUrl` for Aruna's sake, and do not
  `extends` a generated `tsconfig.aruna.json` (that fragment is gone). If `aruna check`
  reports `aruna::111` (alias desync), run `aruna build` or `aruna doctor --fix`.
  Generated output under `generatedDir` is fully owned.
- Schemas are plain immutable objects with zero runtime cost; compose by spreading
  `.shape`, never mutate.
- Bound every string, array, and record an action accepts (`.maxLength`/`.maxChars`,
  `.maxItems`, `.maxEntries`): the compiler warns on unbounded input (`aruna::514`), and
  the bounds go into the contract, where `aruna contract diff` treats a tightened input
  bound as breaking.
- A failure the client should handle by name belongs in the action's `errors`
  (`errors: { OutOfStock: { data: schema.object(...) } }`), thrown with
  `throw ctx.fail("OutOfStock", data)`. On the client, narrow a rejection with
  `isActionError(err, generatedStub, "OutOfStock")` from `aruna/client`; `err.data` is
  then typed. Data that does not match the declaration is masked as `ActionInternalError`.
